note: Ploughshare: the blade of a plow that cuts the soil.

anchor: Who put the French to rout
note: Rout: a crushing defeat in which an army flees in disorder.

anchor: My father lived at Blenheim then
note: Blenheim was a village in Bavaria where, in 1704, an English army under the Duke of Marlborough and Prince Eugène of Savoy defeated the French.

anchor: And many a childing mother then
note: Childing: about to bear a child.

anchor: Great praise the Duke of Marlbro’ won
note: The Duke of Marlborough was the English commander at Blenheim. Parliament built him a great mansion, Blenheim Palace, as a reward.
Prince Eugène of Savoy commanded troops at Blenheim and fought beside Marlborough against the French and Bavarians.
source: Encyclopædia Britannica, 11th ed. (1911), “Marlborough, John Churchill, 1st Duke of”, https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/1911_Encyclop%C3%A6dia_Britannica/Marlborough%2C_John_Churchill%2C_1st_Duke_of

anchor: My days among the Dead are past
note: The Dead: here, the great writers of the past, whom the scholar knows through their books.

anchor: Where’er these casual eyes are cast
With them I take delight in weal

note: Partake: to share in, to take part in.

anchor: My hopes are with the Dead; anon
note: Anon: soon, in a short while.
Futurity: the time to come, the future.
